(u0, else) -> u0
(u1, door_open) -> u2

(u2, at_goal) -> u3
(u2, else) -> u2
(u3, else) -> u3

feedback: The RM is well-formed. Header: FINAL_STATES (u3) is nonempty, u3 is declared and accepting, and u0 is the declared initial state, satisfying the required format. Ordered transition coverage: the progression has_key -> door_open -> at_goal is specified, and every other event in every state is covered by per-state else self-loops ((u0, else), (u1, else), (u2, else), (u3, else)), so irrelevant events such as key_lost have no effect on the machine anywhere. Semantics: u0 -> u1 on has_key correctly captures 'eventually acquire the key'; u1 -> u2 on door_open enforces opening the door after acquiring it; u2 -> u3 on at_goal gives reach the goal after opening. Ordering constraints are respected: door_open cannot precede has_key in the environment, and at_goal cannot precede door_open, so no cheaper shortcut path is rewarded. The task's safety constraint, 'do not drop the key while the door is closed until the door has been opened once', is encoded by the machine structure: any transition out of u1 other than door_open is an else self-loop, so dropping the key (key_lost) while the door is closed leaves the agent in u1 with no penalty trigger needed, and since door_open is required from u1 the agent must be carrying the key (has_key) when the door opens. Dropping after door_open is permitted by the environment and does not block progress since has_key is not rechecked after u1 -> u2. Reachability: u3 is reachable via the documented trace (pickup, toggle, forward). Compactness: four states is minimal for this ordered three-event chain. Reward safety and density: rewards are nonnegative, bounded (max 1.0), and progress rewards of 0.1 and 0.3 are dense shaping between the sparse terminal reward, with the terminal reward of 1.0 dominating so reaching the goal is strictly best. No regression is required by the task since door_open, once achieved from u1, is not required to persist and the RM does not depend on it after u2; the machine remains correct even if the door is later closed, because at_goal is reachable only while the door is open in the environment. Predicate-only events: the RM uses only the four propositions with no fabricated events. Reward function totals match the number of transitions and all reward entries are positive, avoiding degenerate all-zero rewards.
